questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had never been in Asia, NUS is a very good university that offers a wide range of courses and I wanted to travel far from home.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Hard to find anything i would want different

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think it was easy, NUS and KU has a lot of easy accessible information online. However, the information from NUS was at some points a little overwhelming and there was so much that it took a lot of time and effort to make sure that I didn't miss any.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had assistance making sure I could secure the classes I needed, that they didn't overlap and was helped to switch a class despite missing the deadline for the first round (which turned out not to be a problem at all)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: As mentioned, sometimes there was so much information it felt difficult to keep track of everything

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Many. NUS offered different halls, houses, apartments etc to live in. The campus is very big and consists of many different areas. Houses function almost like halls as well, where it is common to share kitchen and bathroom with the people on the same floor as you.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Depends of the type of accommodation. In Pioneer house there were no meal plan but a shared kitchen. I barely used it as there was also a food hall in the area (PGPR) with good, different, and very affordable options. My impression was that most people only use the shared kitchens for breakfast, if any at all.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
My impression is that NUS offer housing for almost all exchange students, if they request wide and different enough options. 
PGPR (one area) has both houses and halls, however the houses are not actual houses, in reality they are the same as halls but with more social activities. Pioneer house is known for being very social with lots of activities. 
If possible try to get a room with AC, to avoid both mold in the room and from getting in clothes etc - and the heat!. If you get a room with no AC, I recommend buying one. Some of the rooms have mold in them, be prepared that it is going to be hard to get the housing services to do anything about it - in my case thet just painted over it. 
However, despite this I want to underline that the housing offered on campus otherwise is great, there is daily cleaning in shared facilities and lots of facilities and activities (gyms, reading rooms, tennis courts, a pool etc.) - and it is very affordable.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Doable, but did take some time and effort - it seems more complicated and overwhelming than it actually is.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: KU helps apply to NUS, then eventually I received a acceptance offer, and from here is had to upload documents such as passport etc., and through their website/platform apply for both housing and classes

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They have guides for everything, almost too many. It is hard to come across anything that NUS does not have a guide for.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesfull, be prepared that not all classes are available for exchange students.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just read through the guides carefully and do not stres too much about it. Try to get in contact with other exchange students from KU, we all helped each other.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The level depends on the type pf class. It is possible to choose what level course you would like before hand: 1000, 2000, 3000 etc. 
I recommend choosing different levels, as it in my opinion was nice with some harder and some more simple.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: NUS requires much more participation during the semester, most classes have attendance and assignments throughout the semester which also counts towards the grades.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
SPH2203 Food Environments, Nutrition & Health: Understanding Key Drivers, Actors and Solutions
MS3216 Gender and Islam
SPH2004 Lifestyle, Behaviour and Public Health
GESS1005 South Asia in Singapore

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I actually loved all my courses, but regards interests I found GESS1005 South Asia in Singapore very nice in terms of gaining knowledge about Singapore and South asian culture when visiting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not so much unexpected, but spend some on travlling as I had room in my budget for it.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was very cheap in both food halls and hawker kitchens (street kitchens) - I barely ate anywhere else.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't really use a lot of them - but there were lots.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: NUS is a large university offering almost anything you can think of

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I loved using the facilities such as tennis courts, pools and gyms

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Taiwan if possible. Otherwise it is easy to travel to Malaysia and some Indonesian islands

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, everyone was very welcoming.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: If you want to socialize, try to get accommodation in a house. They have lots of activities almost every week.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Adjusting to the climate in the beginning.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: In the end the climate, but also the people and how it is very safe everywhere. I was never worried walking alone at night, even as a female.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Try to get in contact with the other students going, plan some trips during the semester and be open to meet new people.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not very specific, but I absolutely loved my exchange semester and I couldn’t think of any better place than Singapore and NUS. I would change a thing about it, and I am very grateful I ended up going.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My new friends and my insights in Asian culture

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being very far from home on bad days, but I could just as well have bad days in Denmark.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
